reviews.text:
I don't understand the point of making a reservation. Despite arriving earlier than my reservation time, I ended up waiting for an hour.

What's the point of making a reservation if this is the case?

I'm extremely dissatisfied because I wasn't informed about the waiting time beforehand.
After comparing the receipt with the blood test results, I realized I had been ripped off.

My beloved dog was previously diagnosed with "immunodeficiency" at this animal hospital, and I visited the clinic monthly for a year. Each visit cost between 100,000 and 200,000 yen, but my dog's condition didn't improve at all; he became so emaciated that his spine was visible.

I gave him medication daily, took him to the hospital every month, and sometimes he was even hospitalized. The doctor told me that "immunodeficiency is an incurable disease, so he'll have to take medication for the rest of his life," and I desperately followed the doctor's instructions to prevent my dog's condition from worsening.

Then, I consulted my mother, a former veterinary nurse, about the situation, and she pointed out that "something seemed a little off." I decided to get a second opinion, and received a completely different diagnosis: my dog ​​did not have immunodeficiency.

Furthermore, when I stopped giving him the daily medication, my dog's condition improved dramatically. His appetite returned, and his emaciated body returned to normal. Afterward, I visited another animal hospital, but no immune disorders were found.


Also, when I used the pet hotel attached to this hospital, my pet would sometimes return injured or extremely exhausted when I went to pick it up. Since then, I've lost faith in other pet hotels and still don't use them.

This hospital had many positive reviews and ratings at the time, so I thought it was trustworthy and went there regularly. However, I felt a strong sense of profit motive, which grew my distrust. At the time, I was only 19 years old, and looking back, I think I was taken advantage of by the hospital.

I will never go to this hospital again, but if anyone else is experiencing similar anxieties, I strongly encourage you to consider getting a second opinion. I wrote this review hoping it might be helpful to someone.

Previously, I had a trusting experience with this female dermatologist after she examined my dog's dermatitis, which my regular vet couldn't find the cause of, and it was completely cured.

This year, on a day when my regular vet was closed, a male veterinarian called and said he could see my dog ​​immediately. I went to this clinic right away.
I was informed that tumor removal surgery was necessary and was scheduled for the near future, but I asked for an estimate of the surgery fee just in case. It was more than three times the price of other clinics (around 150,000-160,000 yen → 450,000-500,000 yen).
When I mentioned that it was quite expensive compared to the online market price I had researched (150,000-200,000 yen), he replied, "That's because it includes a pathology examination."

Other clinics quoted 150,000-160,000 yen including the pathology examination.

Is this a commission system?

While the reception staff and each specialist veterinarian were polite, I felt distrustful of the price, which deviated significantly from the market rate, even if it's a negotiated price system. Other clinics were also surprised by the price.

Unless it's an emergency where you can't wait even a day, if you have time to consider treatment options, it's important to get quotes from other clinics and carefully choose a hospital and veterinarian.

I chose this clinic because it was open on a Sunday night and is well-known in the neighborhood and always crowded.

It's incredibly expensive... way too expensive!

A stool test alone cost 27,500 yen?! The doctor said it would be around 20,000 yen, but it was almost 30,000 yen.

The medication costs were also higher than other clinics, and I was surprised by the huge difference in price for medication.

I only took my pet there once, and I visited three times for test results and other things, paying around 70,000 yen in total.

My pet hasn't gotten better yet, and I want to continue taking him, but the cost is so frightening that I'm thinking of switching hospitals.

I recommend checking the costs carefully before getting any tests or medication prescribed.

I used their temporary cat boarding service, but I was left with serious concerns about hygiene management and staff conduct.

The website stated that "vaccination" and "flea and tick prevention" were mandatory, so I brought my vaccination certificate.

However, they didn't check it at all until I presented it. I'm worried about whether the other cats boarded there are truly protected.

Also, despite requesting flea and tick prevention when dropping off my cat, I was told at the time of payment, "We forgot, would you like us to do it now?" which was very surprising. If mandatory procedures are so ineffective (or easily forgotten), I wouldn't have left my cat there in the first place.

Furthermore, the "free health check" mentioned on the website was not performed. The discrepancy between the pre-arranged information and the actual service is too great, and I don't feel it's an environment where I can confidently leave my beloved pet. I strongly hope for improvements in the future.

Other reviews mentioned the receptionist was unfriendly, and indeed, she's not exactly friendly.

They often leave you alone unless you initiate contact.

Some people say this place is expensive, but I used to go to an even more expensive place.

However, I didn't trust the doctor there, so I came here.

I think the doctor examines patients well.

They also explain things in detail.

I only go on the days when the same doctor is on duty, so I've only met two doctors so far, but both were good.

They even called me before the spaying/neutering surgery, asking, "Given this situation, is it okay to proceed with this test?" They made sure to confirm everything.

It's a bit of a distance from my home, but I think I've found a good doctor.

There are plenty of veterinarians, which is reassuring, but the reception is incredibly slow and unfriendly. I've been there many times, but it's been particularly bad lately. Even after the examination is over, I have to wait twice as long to pay. I appreciate that they reimburse me for an hour of parking, but it never finishes in an hour. If you look closely, they're handling both the calculations and the new patient registration at the same time, and even though there are two staff members, both stop what they're doing to help. They're incredibly inefficient. Please improve.

My 7-year-old, who is otherwise healthy, visited the clinic after accidentally swallowing a dental wipe.

I only wanted them to induce vomiting, but after explaining the risks of accidental ingestion, they suggested taking two X-rays (approximately 3000 yen each) before and after vomiting, citing the possibility of other foreign objects being present and the risk of choking during vomiting.

I initially declined, but they explained it again in a separate room and seemed to strongly urge me to do so.

Ultimately, we did not have the X-rays done, and the treatment (injection, IV drip, oral medication) cost approximately 15,000 yen. If we had had the X-rays, it would have cost nearly 30,000 yen, just to get the wipes vomited.

I checked with other clinics and acquaintances about similar cases, and they were surprised that the cost was somewhat high for this procedure. Of course, I understand that it was a precautionary measure, but the wipes don't show up on X-rays (confirmed with the nurse). I found it difficult to judge what level of testing was truly necessary. After inducing vomiting, my child was given anti-nausea medication, dehydration prevention medication, and stomach medicine. I was given an explanation and felt I had no right to refuse. Looking at the receipt, I see that charges were incurred for everything. If they were going to be so attentive, I wish they had consulted me beforehand.

Previously, when my child had bloody stools and I was surprised and took them to the doctor, they suggested tests and medication costing 20,000-30,000 yen. After doing some research myself, I learned that bloody stools can sometimes be psychogenic, so I declined, saying I would wait a day to see how things went. I felt some doubt about prescribing medication without knowing the cause, and in that case, observation led to improvement. Considering that, I wanted to think more carefully this time.

Regarding the necessity of tests and treatments, I recommend not being swayed on the spot, but carefully checking the content and costs before making a decision.
I was very surprised that they didn't give me the vaccination even though I went to the hospital with vaccination as my top priority, and they didn't explain the costs or anything like that.

I had been going there for a long time and liked it so much that I would recommend it to others, but the doctor's attitude suddenly changed, so I stopped going. (Perhaps they couldn't handle my case anymore, because they told me to go to another animal hospital.) I also don't think the pet hotel is a very clean environment. Although they don't let you see it in person, the cage my pet was in when I picked it up was very unsanitary. The waiting time is also long, and just waiting is tiring.

My regular doctor was closed, so they rushed me in. They were very courteous. However, I was surprised at how expensive it was. I paid the same amount for the consultation as I would have paid for surgery at my regular doctor's office. I was shocked. But thanks to them, my dog ​​recovered safely, so thank you very much.

While this is the owner's problem,
it was crowded with multiple visitors,
and there were animals and owners waiting outside,
and I wondered why the hospital didn't pay any attention to it, leaving sick animals to wait in the cold.
(When I asked where I should wait, they said either the waiting room or outside. The receptionist was surly and irritable, and wouldn't answer unless I asked, so I thought she wasn't suited to being a receptionist.)

It was helpful that they were open on holidays,
but I wondered if it was okay for just 2-3 people to take up seats in the waiting room.
I thought the general etiquette of the pet owners was poor.

The examination involved kidney problems, but the possibility of allergies was also raised, and the examination didn't address that...
As a result, my entire face was swollen when I got home, I coughed all night, and I spent about 7,000 yen on a pointless consultation.
I realized how important it is to find a hospital that's open on holidays.

It's well-known and has good reviews. It's a little pricey, but they provide excellent care, and the doctor listened to me directly when I called for the first time. I have a cat, and I thought it might have FIP, so I took him there. Other hospitals say they can't tell, but they really explain things in detail, so I feel at ease. My cats don't mind going to the hospital.
I would not recommend it.

I've been treated here many times.
All the doctors are polite and explain things thoroughly.
Even when I went to other emergency hospitals at night and couldn't find a solution, I was able to get treatment here quickly.
Some people have written that the fees are high, but I think that's unavoidable given the doctors' high diagnostic and treatment skills. (Pets do cost money to treat, after all.)
It's always crowded, which shows how popular it is.

Other doctors told me to give up on treating my beloved cat's malignant lymphoma, but this doctor patiently explained everything from the beginning and did everything he could to help us. He's a truly kind and wonderful doctor! I highly recommend this hospital and doctor as your family vet!

There was no explanation of the costs, and the 6-day hospitalization cost 400,000 yen. It's disappointing that there was absolutely no prior consultation.

My dog ​​was hospitalized for 6 days with pulmonary edema.

While I'm grateful for the treatment itself, I'm very concerned about the complete lack of explanation regarding the costs from the head veterinarian, and I wanted to share my experience.

- No estimate or cost guideline provided before hospitalization.
- No consultation regarding the treatment plan, such as "how far should we go?"
- No explanation of when additional costs might arise.
- I only learned the total cost was approximately 400,000 yen upon discharge.

Afterward, I sought second and third opinions at other hospitals, and was told,

"This price is quite high for what was done," and "It's usually about half that price."

I understand that saving a life is the top priority, but as a pet owner, I can't make a decision without prior explanation.

I don't want to refuse treatment; I just wish there had been some prior explanation or options presented so I could have entrusted my dog ​​to them with peace of mind.

Because they advertise so much and have so many doctors, I couldn't help but suspect they have some kind of sales quota... I felt they were incredibly lacking in explanation.

I'm now using a different hospital, and I trust them completely because they thoroughly explain things like:
- Confirmation of cost limits
- Explanation of treatment details
- Discussion of additional tests

I wrote this as a warning to other dog owners who care deeply for their pets, so they don't get surprised by a sudden, exorbitant bill like I did.
It was my first time at this hospital, and the doctor was kind and explained everything thoroughly, which was great, but unfortunately the receptionist was unfriendly and provided poor service.

WM Partners Co., Ltd. managed the WM Growth Fund No. 5 Limited Partnership, which invested in December 2022. This capital alliance featured a growth strategy and established a secondary veterinary care facility specialising in treating dogs and cats. The management structure was refined to allow the director to concentrate on clinical practice.

Thank you for your continued support. I found a kitten with a difficult-to-treat skin condition, and other hospitals were unable to help until I found this clinic. You've been patiently caring for her. It's also conveniently located near my home, which is a great help.

The service is polite and kind; they conduct a thorough consultation before each examination after check-in. Because it's a popular clinic, the wait time for the first visit is very long. After that, they don't take appointments; it's first-come, first-served, so if you go late, the wait is long.

However, as with other animal hospitals, popular clinics often don't take appointments and see patients in the order they arrive.

I think this is because there are emergencies and the time required for each consultation is unpredictable.

I believe this is because they treat each patient carefully, so I have no complaints. Even for my regular check-ups, they don't rush through the process; they listen carefully to what I have to say, which makes me feel at ease bringing my pet here.

Some other reviews mention the high cost, but I've been to several other hospitals, and some were cheap but not thorough, while others were expensive but provided inadequate treatment. I'm happy with the price because I feel I'm getting a good examination here. It really comes down to personal preference and how you feel about the hospital.

Crowd Level:
Weekend mornings are the busiest, but if you line up a few tens of minutes before the hospital opens, you're likely to be seen sooner (though this varies). *First-time patients usually have a long wait.

Weekday afternoons are relatively quiet. It gets crowded in the evenings, though.

They hardly ever close, so it's helpful that they're open every day, even in case of sudden illness.

My child has a difficult illness, but they always treat us carefully, which is very reassuring. Thank you. We look forward to continuing to use your services.

I really appreciate that you're open on holidays and late into the night.

When my uterus became infected with abscesses, you performed surgery and saved my life, even though it was right before closing time.

For a minor anal gland rupture, you carefully explained the options—suturing, topical medication—and the costs and physical burden involved.

Thank you for always providing such thorough care.

I'm a local resident.

Could you please stop parking so casually on the street in front of the hospital?

Not only are you bothering the people using the road, but don't you realize you're blocking one of the two lanes?

You might think that as long as it's convenient for you, you don't care about others, but it's causing a lot of trouble.

That road isn't yours.

I found an online search for first-time consultations and decided to come here, probably because I lived in Kamiroku as a child. The doctors and staff were all friendly, and after seeing the dermatologist in charge, my dog's skin condition improved dramatically around July. I immediately switched my 4-year-old male toy poodle to Amino Acid Doctor Care Potato and oral ointment, and he recovered in about a month and a half, so I'm very happy. I was worried about what would happen in the hot and humid heat, but he has improved dramatically...He still needs to take oral medication with a gap in between, but his condition has improved significantly. I was so happy that I decided to review this.

It was about 10 years ago, but I took my dog ​​to the head veterinarian. He diagnosed that surgery was necessary, but I was bothered by the way he explained things. When I said I wanted some time to think, he seemed to be pressuring me to schedule the surgery, saying things like, "If you don't do it, there's a chance he might die, are you sure? It would be cruel not to do everything you can." In the end, I decided against the surgery and went to two other hospitals (one for a consultation only), but both determined that surgery wasn't necessary. My dog ​​recovered with oral medication.

Recently, my daughter told me she had a similar experience at this hospital (I'm not sure if it was the head veterinarian), and it brought back memories and made me very angry.

I understand that they're not a charity and they want to make a profit. However, I think they should stop using language that exploits a pet owner's feelings for their pet.

It seems like this hospital has been acquired by M&A.
Maybe they're overwhelmed with debt?

Either way, I will never have my beloved dog treated at this hospital again.
I can't go into details, but I've come to realise how important a second opinion is.

They explained clearly what tests and treatments would be needed, but
when additional tests were needed, they did so without my permission. I know veterinary clinics are expensive, and I brought a fair amount of supplies, but I would have liked a confirmation or word of warning beforehand.

This is just my personal opinion, but...
It's so sad.
I'm truly heartbroken.
Despite advertising itself as an oncology department,
the patient couldn't even get an appointment with the freelance doctor who only sees them twice a month.
And passed away less than a week after the surgery.
All that's left is what should have been a three-digit figure for the surgery.

I'm truly heartbroken.

I was suffering from severe itching and hadn't seen any improvement even after going to other hospitals, but just as the reviews said, my symptoms have subsided here. A female doctor with extensive skin knowledge took the time to counsel me and, after examining my calluses, quickly identified the cause. She explained things clearly so that even someone as ignorant as me could understand, and I was very impressed by her advice not to force me onto medication.

The consultation fee was also reasonable, which gave me peace of mind. It's not close to my home, but I'm happy to have found a good hospital that's worth the trip.

I look forward to continuing to work with you.

I had been going to this hospital for some time.

I knew the treatment costs were clearly higher than at other hospitals,
but it was close to my home, so I continued to go there and felt reassured if something happened.

The doctor in charge always spoke with a confident tone,
so I believed him and entrusted his treatment to my beloved dog.

However, the symptoms did not improve at all, and I became anxious,
so I visited two other veterinary hospitals. Both doctors were surprised and asked me why I was receiving such treatment.

It was at that moment that I realized the treatment I was receiving there was clearly off the mark.

I still regret not visiting a different hospital sooner.

I strongly felt that in order to protect the lives of my precious family members,
it is extremely important to get a second or third opinion,
even at a familiar hospital.

I will never use this hospital again.

I urge anyone considering visiting this hospital to make a careful decision.

Three years ago, my 6-month-old toy poodle became unwell and I took him here. The doctor was friendly and kind, but when I expressed concern because his condition never improved, he would always say, "I'm not treating him alone; I work as a team with other doctors, so don't worry!"

At each appointment, I was required to undergo various tests, which were expensive. Finally, he said, "We won't know the cause unless we do an endoscopic examination." I was very worried, considering the burden on the puppy, but I had no choice but to undergo the examination. The test results showed an "unknown cause."

Even after all the tests, the cause remained unclear, and I thought there was no hope for him, so I moved to another hospital. I was relieved to find out the diagnosis there, with fewer tests and at a reasonable cost.

If you're a regular patient at Uehonmachi Animal Hospital, I recommend not following the advice to undergo the tests you're told to. It's hard to deny that they prioritize making money.

Since your pet is an important member of your family, I recommend taking these cases into consideration, carefully examining your pet, and even considering getting a second opinion. I posted this in the hope that it might be helpful to someone.

I had visited four other clinics before finally finding this hospital on my fifth visit.

At the time, the clinic was run by a single doctor. It all started when a friend recommended this clinic to me, as my rescue dog wasn't getting any better despite trying everything else.

He wouldn't eat, his paws were swollen, and he was diagnosed with a very complicated illness: a rabies vaccine allergy, an autoimmune disease, and lymphocytic plasmacytic enteritis. He was about 1 year and 2 months old when we found out. At the time, we were told that he might not live past 5 years old with this disease.

Sometimes I went every month, and sometimes every week.

For me, moving and being single meant traveling from another prefecture, but the competent doctors and assistants made it manageable.

My beloved dog continued his battle with illness, even while I adopted other rescue dogs. He crossed the Rainbow Bridge on March 10, 2025, but he lived to be 13 years old and died peacefully of old age without much suffering.

This was the third time I had lost a dog. It was such a sudden event, especially since we'd just taken him to the vet the day before, fed him, and gone for a walk. I called the hospital, and I'm truly grateful to the director, doctors, nurses, and reception staff—everyone was so caring and understanding, sharing my feelings with them.

Thank you for always laughing at Kinta's clumsiness.

I visited many large 24-hour medical centers and numerous well-known hospitals, but none were as caring as this one. Honestly, I believe a good animal hospital is about the compatibility between the owner and the veterinarian, and how much you can entrust your pet's life to them.

My beloved dog never hated going to the hospital; he was always excited at the entrance. I'm so happy we were able to build such a trusting relationship with Uehonmachi Animal Hospital.

I've recommended it to several friends, and they all said they never thought someone as clueless as me would know about such a wonderful hospital.

Thank you always, Director, Dr. Nakao, and Dr. Sugiyama. We look forward to your continued support.

I am truly grateful to Ms. M, Ms. O, and everyone else who has since retired for their prompt and efficient service.

My dog ​​was so fortunate to have met you all.

In my opinion, this is the hospital I would recommend first and foremost to anyone who may get a pet in the future—myself, my family, and my friends.

Thank you so much.

When my kitten was about six months old, its belly became bloated, and it seemed less energetic and less active than its siblings. I took it to a local veterinary clinic, where it was immediately diagnosed with FIP. A definitive diagnostic test was performed, and I was told the results would be available in a week. When I got home and did some research, I learned that some kittens die within a week. The clinic said they couldn't treat it, so I immediately looked for a clinic that could treat it and came here. Dr. Nakao examined my kitten, and oral medication treatment began. Dr. Nakao explained the medication, the treatment plan, the possibility of recurrence, and what to expect after treatment in great detail, which allowed me to face the treatment with peace of mind. After 84 days of oral medication treatment, there has been no recurrence, and it is completely different from before the treatment. It can now play and get into mischief with its siblings, and I am very grateful. Thank you very much.

This hospital has saved my child's life so many times.
They provide thorough examinations.
We are truly grateful that they are open on weekends and holidays. This hospital is indispensable to us.

When I first visited Uehonmachi Animal Hospital, I was put at ease by the warm welcome from all the staff.

The long consultation hours, until 8 PM even on weekends and holidays, were extremely helpful, making it easy to visit after work or on my days off.

My dog ​​sometimes gets sick in the evenings, so this was a great help.

The doctor was very caring and explained my dog's symptoms thoroughly,
alleviating my anxieties completely.

The availability of specialized clinics for dermatology and oncology is particularly reassuring,
and the ability to receive specialized treatment is a major advantage.

The hospital is clean and well-equipped, making it a place where I can confidently entrust my dog.

I would definitely recommend it to other pet owners.

Since moving here, I have been treated for skin problems for my dog. 

It was my first time dealing with a skin disease, and even after searching online I didn't know what to do and was very anxious, but the receptionists were kind and the doctor was as calm as you'd expect. 

Perhaps sensing my situation, he also gave me a thorough explanation that was easy to understand. 

They seem to treat a wide range of subjects and are open until 8pm every night, so I feel this is a hospital I can trust to leave my dog ​​to if something happens in the future.

I think this is a very good clinic.
My dog ​​suddenly became lethargic while we were out, and I rushed him in for an examination, but they were able to calm him down.
During the examination, they took a thorough explanation based on my questions about his past history and test results, and they were very gentle with my pet.
The nurses were also very attentive despite being busy, so I'm very satisfied.

I used to travel an hour round trip to a hospital for each checkup, but considering my dog's age, I was looking for a closer clinic and decided to go with this one.

The atmosphere is wonderful, the doctor and staff are kind and attentive, and my dog ​​has become very attached to them. (He's still scared of injections, though, haha!)

It's a very comfortable environment to discuss any concerns I might have, and I'm very grateful. Thank you.
The veterinarian and staff are all very kind and attentive, and provide compassionate care. …

Our 10-year-old Shiba Inu has been a patient here for several years. Perhaps because he's used to it, I've never seen any dogs making a fuss here. The stylists are all very kind to both people and animals. …

I'm always grateful for your help.

The teachers and reception staff are all very polite and helpful.
Doctors provide loving care that takes your pet's feelings into consideration. A heartfelt animal hospital where owners can leave their pets in peace!
Kind and courteous!
